From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [INC-6298] Dedicated pool congestion impacting BrightHealth dedicated nodes

Team —

We started seeing sustained GPU utilization spikes on the BrightHealth dedicated pool at 02:03 UTC (approx 09:03 PST) and by 02:11 UTC the scheduler reported queue growth that exceeded our preferred headroom. Impacted model: redwood-16k-v2 (quantized). Symptoms: 95–100% GPU utilization on 6/8 reserved nodes; token latencies spiked 3–6x for BrightHealth routed requests.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Auto-fallback: routed new BrightHealth requests to the hosted compatibility variant at 02:15 UTC (warmup observed).
- Throttling: temporary per-user qps limit applied at 02:18 UTC to preserve API responsiveness.
- Emergency burst allocation: brought two burst nodes online and drained the most loaded hosts by 02:36 UTC.

Current status: capacity pressure subsided by 03:05 UTC after burst and routing; no sustained errors seen since 03:20 UTC. We still need to finalize root cause (suspected combination of a new batch job + atypical prefix cache behavior).

Action items for comms:
- Customer message (clear timeline + mitigations + offer) — Marissa to draft.
- CS coordination for invoice/credit hold — Monica.
- Technical postmortem + RCA — I'll lead and draft by EOD tomorrow.

Attaching initial extraction of scheduler logs and a short timeline to the incident folder.

-sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood Inference — Dedicated pool congestion on 2026-12-15 (summary & next steps)

Hi Sam / BrightHealth team —

I’m reaching from Redwood on behalf of our engineering and SRE teams. We want to apologize for the degraded performance you saw this morning against your dedicated capacity and provide a short timeline, what we did to mitigate, and next steps.

What happened (short):
- 02:03 UTC: SRE observed sustained GPU utilization on your dedicated pool, leading to queue growth and increased latency for your API calls.
- 02:15–02:36 UTC: We applied a sequence of mitigations (automatic fallback to hosted compatibility variant, per-tenant throttling, and emergency burst nodes).
- 03:05 UTC: Observed return to baseline latency; no further degradation detected since 03:20 UTC.

Immediate steps we took:
- Rerouted new requests to a hosted variant to reduce load on your reserved nodes.
- Temporarily limited request rate from your tenancy to stabilize tail latency.
- Provisioned two burst nodes and redistributed traffic away from overloaded hosts.

What we’re investigating:
- Initial signs point to an overlap of a scheduled high-throughput batch job with an unexpected cache miss pattern that increased per-request compute. We will validate whether an autoscaling threshold or scheduler handoff contributed.
- Full RCA and remediation plan to follow (root cause, fix, and long-term guardrails).

Our proposed customer actions and offer:
- We propose a pro-rated service credit for the impacted window (02:03–03:05 UTC) — see attached credit-proposal-BH-4392.xlsx for the calculation.
- As a gesture of goodwill, we’re offering one month of free peak burst credits for Dedicated to help smooth any near-term capacity spikes while we complete fixes.
- We’d like to schedule a 30–45 minute technical session with your eng team to walk through the timeline and prevent recurrence. Are you available 16/17 Dec (your local times)?

Attachments: incident-timeline-20261215.pdf; credit-proposal-BH-4392.xlsx

Again, I’m sorry for the disruption. Monica will reach out separately on the credit calculation and billing hold.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
